pairs.why: Both calculators have the same tilted body with a key grid that follows the face reasonably well; the only real difference is key color, not construction.
A's labeled keypad sits on rows that follow the tilted face, while B's blank, nearly uniform keys and strongly rotated body make a calculator that can't do its job and has a weaker key layout.
A is a wall clock hanging flat against the wall with a consistent rim ellipse, while B's round clock stands on its rim on the floor with no stand or base to hold it up.
A's lifebuoy hangs from a hook on a corner post and the deck planks recede consistently onto supported posts, while B's lifebuoy floats in front of the deck edge with unclear attachment.
B is a wall clock mounted flat with a consistent rim, while A's round clock stands upright on the floor on its rim with nothing supporting it.
A's coil lies flat on the ground with the loop rising from it and the bindings holding everything together, while B's coil and ring stand upright edge-on like eyeglasses, which loose rope cannot do.

A's X-braced legs pivot at a bolt under the seat and support the armrests and back as a believable folding camp chair, while B's back posts and X legs join the seat ambiguously and its pivot sits off-center.
B's coil and loop are drawn as tilted ellipses lying in one plane on the ground, while A's coil and ring stand vertically face-on like rigid hoops, which rope can't hold.
